record_identity.title: Defensive–offensive autonomy scope compression and control coupling

summary: A governance failure in which defensive interception and offensive force are represented, controlled, or disabled through one undifferentiated military-autonomy category, causing an offensive safeguard to disable independently authorised bounded protection or allowing a defensive exception to propagate into offensive authority.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: CAM already distinguishes ETH.UFC-DI defensive interception from ETH.UFC-OS offensive targeting. Without an explicit non-propagation and control-scope rule, that semantic distinction may collapse at the authority or control layer. The result can either remove continuity-safe protection when offensive autonomy is suspended or carry time-compressed defensive authority into retaliatory, pursuit, target-selection, or other offensive action.

failure_mode_definition: A governance failure occurs where defensive interception and offensive force are represented, controlled, suspended, overridden, or disabled through one undifferentiated military-autonomy category, such that a safeguard intended to constrain offensive force also disables independently authorised bounded defensive protection, or a defensive exception, state, or control path propagates into offensive authority.
failure_threshold: The threshold is met when a control or authority representation fails to preserve the operationally relevant distinction between bounded defensive interception and offensive targeting or strike, and that compression either changes the availability of independently authorised defensive protection or expands the authority available for offensive force. Merely using a common policy vocabulary, shared operator interface, or coordinated command structure does not meet the threshold if distinct authority, expiry, override, continuity, and audit semantics remain effective.

failure_classification.likelihood: structurally plausible where systems or controls compress military autonomy into one scope; no real-world occurrence identified
failure_classification.confidence: high for the pre-repair Caelestis corpus gap; moderate for structural relevance; unverified for real-world occurrence
affected_rights_or_interests: lawful and attributable use of force
failure_classification.failure_scope: military and use-of-force authority architectures containing defensive and offensive functions
failure_classification.recurrence_pattern: May recur whenever policy, interfaces, emergency controls, or autonomy shutdowns treat distinct force postures as one operative category.
failure_classification.persistence: Persists while authority and controls lack explicit non-propagation and scope-preservation requirements.
failure_classification.reproducibility: Can be tested with controlled disable, suspend, override, threat-envelope, and exception-propagation scenarios without using live weapons.
failure_classification.visibility: May be hidden until a broad control is activated or a defensive exception crosses an authority boundary.
failure_classification.severity_assessment_basis: S1 reflects credible high-consequence pathways involving either loss of time-critical defensive protection or unauthorised propagation into offensive force. The rating relies on foreseeable deployment harm and a verified governance gap, not on an observed real-world incident.
failure_classification.severity_assessment_gap: No public incident demonstrates that one shared control disabled an offensive AI system and an air-defence system or propagated authority between them.
